own_solution.law: Energy balance for sensible heating: P t = m c Delta T, so t = m c Delta T / P
assumptions: all 1500 W goes into the water (no losses, negligible container heat capacity)
no phase change over the 40 K rise

T47A8.regime: liquid water throughout: T0 > 273.15 K and T0 + 40 K < 373.15 K (at 1 atm); 293 K -> 333 K is inside

T17E2.regime: liquid water throughout: T0 > 273.15 K and T0 + 40 K < 373.15 K (at 1 atm); 293 K -> 333 K is inside

notes: t = 2*4186*40/1500 = 334880/1500 = 223.25 s. With the extra 1 kg mixed in (same starting temperature, so no change in initial temperature): t = 3*4186*40/1500 = 334.88 s. Paired sentences state the same values (293 K; 1 kg). The jug sentences say 'the same starting temperature' although the base problem does not state a starting temperature; this is harmless because only equality matters. The no-loss assumption is implicit ('delivers 1500 W to the water'), which is standard.
